objective: Gate leading-edge calls by one Date.now timestamp, including exact boundaries and consumed error/reentry windows.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Leading-edge throttling remains a practical event-handling technique.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Rate-limiting a synchronous callback requires a clear eligibility window.
relevanceRationale.transferable: State-before-callback and exact boundary comparisons generalize to guards.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A bounded nondecreasing clock and argument model keep scope explicit.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Reset-timer queue order and callback errors can leave a wrapper blocked.

defects: Junior installed its reset timer after fn, so a thrown callback permanently blocked later calls.
Timer-reset junior disagreed with the timestamp skeleton at eligibility boundaries.
Reference read Date.now twice for one accepted call; opaque arguments and return/error contracts were unspecified.
rationale: Use one timestamp read and store-before-callback in reference/junior, retaining the existing timestamp senior. Explicitly author Date.now-based eligibility rather than reset timers, exact >= boundary, unchanged drop stamp, nonnegative nondecreasing integer clock values and receiver-independent exact opaque arguments. A thrown callback consumes the window but propagates its original value. Add synchronously restored local clock fixtures for zero/exact/just-before boundaries, drop non-extension, reentry, original errors/identities and 10000 accepted calls; retained real-time cases still test no trailing replay.
